approach: Write the height at time t using the launch speed and g, express the launch speed with H and T, then rewrite the height using H and T alone.

steps.text: Since the particle reaches maximum height H at time T, the launch speed is u = gT. Write the height at any time t.
Express H using u and g, then substitute u = gT.
Take option d and expand it to check whether it equals y(t).
steps.equation: H − ½g(T − t)² = ½gT² − ½g(T² − 2Tt + t²) = gTt − ½gt²

steps.text: This matches y(t) exactly, so option d is the correct expression for the height at time t.

common_mistakes.text: Dropping the factor of ½ while expanding H − ½g(T − t)², giving H − g(T − t)², which is a different, smaller expression.
Writing only the offset-from-the-top term ½g(T − t)² and forgetting to subtract it from H, which gives the distance fallen from the top, not the height above the ground.
